tasks.short: Work through on-site troubleshooting, request help from the vendor's technical service centre, explain the fault and steps tried, fix it with the support engineer, and note the case on the work order.

steps.what: Telecom technician works through the on-site troubleshooting procedures first

Telecom technician requests support from the technical service centre: by phone with a wait in the queue today; after the change by writing a portal request with the steps tried, readings, logs and photos
Telecom technician checks the final request: fault description, steps tried, readings, attachments and the vendor contract it goes to
Telecom technician submits the checked request on the vendor portal
Telecom technician explains the problem, readings and steps tried to the support engineer
Telecom technician works through the fix with the support engineer
Telecom technician notes the support case number and outcome on the work order

tasks.design: From the work order in the field service app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) the technician writes a support request on the vendor's portal ({PARTNER_PORTAL}) with the steps tried, readings, device logs and photos attached, checks it and submits it once, and gets a call back instead of waiting in a phone queue. The support engineer reads the attachments first, so less is explained by phone. The case number links back to the work order. Troubleshooting and fixing stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Support was phoned, with long queues and everything explained aloud.
tasks.enabler_now: Vendor portals take support cases with logs and photos and call back.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent outages still need the phone line.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which detail the support engineer needs first.

evidence.claim: Equipment vendors run support portals that take cases with attached logs and photos.
Workflow systems that can track staff need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the fault ticket to the updated work order; vendor repairs at their site are outside.
Input contract: fault tickets from the network operations centre; vendor portal access under the support contract; fallback is the phone line.

Troubleshooting, fixing, the request check and the submit keep their full time. s2 keeps 60 because the queue wait goes and writing the request with its attachments takes most of the rest; s3 keeps 70 because the engineer has read the attachments; s5 keeps 60 because the case number links itself and the outcome is still written.
The vendor's time is outside the technician's savings.

incremental.description: No new upkeep: attaching logs and photos is part of writing the request in s2.

approvals.approved_version: The support request with fault description, steps tried, readings, logs and photos exactly as checked by the technician in s2c, submitted once on the vendor's portal under the support contract; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about half of cases go to vendors with a portal and call-back, so the rest stay on the phone line (8.6); high: the main vendors take portal cases (17.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Test cable pairs or fibres, check the cable records for assignments, designate free cables and label them, and update the cable records.

steps.what: Telecom technician tests cable pairs or fibres for faults
Telecom technician checks the paper cable records for assigned pairs
Telecom technician designates cables available for use and labels them
Telecom technician updates the cable records: on paper sheets today, in the inventory system on the tablet after the change

tasks.design: Cable assignments live in the network inventory system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) on the technician's tablet, which shows which pairs or fibres are free on each cable. The technician records test results and designations there on site instead of on paper sheets. Testing, designating and labelling stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cable records were paper sheets in the exchange, updated by hand and often out of date.
tasks.enabler_now: Network inventory systems hold cable and pair assignments on tablets.
tasks.still_hard: Records are only as good as the last person who updated them.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a pair marked free that is clearly in use.

reach.learn: Whether current records cut failed connections.

evidence.claim: Network inventory systems hold cable, pair and fibre assignments and show free capacity.

assumptions: Boundary: from the cable request to the cable records; connecting customers is outside.
Input contract: cable requests from the network planner; current assignments in the inventory system; fallback is paper sheets.

Testing, designating and labelling keep their full time. s2 keeps 60 for reading the free pairs and checking doubtful ones; s4 keeps 85 because pairs are picked from the list instead of written out, and test results and designations are still entered by the technician.
Paper records are migrated once by the network planning team.

incremental.description: Telecom technician corrects records found wrong on site.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the exchange's records are still being migrated, so most look-ups stay on paper (2.5); high: current digital records (10.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Note the equipment's alarm or error code, find the matching troubleshooting section in the manufacturer's manual, check the manual fits the firmware, and follow the maintenance instructions.

steps.what: Telecom technician notes the alarm or error code shown by the equipment
Telecom technician refers to manufacturers' manuals for the troubleshooting section on that code
Telecom technician checks the manual's revision matches the equipment firmware
Telecom technician follows the maintenance instructions for the specific malfunction step by step

tasks.design: The element manager ({OPS_SYSTEM}) passes the equipment's error code, model and firmware version to the work order, and a lookup table opens the manufacturer's troubleshooting procedure for that code and firmware in the vendor portal ({PARTNER_PORTAL}). No model is involved; the link is by code. Following the instructions stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Codes were read off the panel and looked up in long manuals, sometimes for the wrong firmware.
tasks.enabler_now: Element managers report codes and firmware; vendor portals index procedures by code.
tasks.still_hard: Faults without a code still need the full manual.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when the manual's procedure will take down a live service.

evidence.claim: Vendor portals index troubleshooting procedures by error code and firmware version.

assumptions: Boundary: from the malfunction to the fix; parts ordering is outside.
Input contract: error codes and firmware from the element manager; procedures from the vendor portal under the support contract; fallback is the manual.
Following the instructions does not change.
The code table is kept by the technical support team.
unknowns: Share of faults with an error code.

incremental.description: Telecom technician reports codes with no linked procedure.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly older equipment without an element manager, so codes are read and manuals searched by hand (9.2); high: newer equipment that reports code and firmware (28.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect test readings and printouts, read trouble reports, compare readings with normal values and earlier tests, analyze them to decide repair needs and methods, and write the repair plan.

steps.what: Telecom technician collects test readings and computer printouts for the fault
Telecom technician reads trouble reports from customers and the help desk
Telecom technician compares readings with normal values and earlier tests
Telecom technician analyzes test readings and trouble reports to determine equipment repair needs and required repair methods
Telecom technician writes the repair plan on the work order

tasks.design: The network management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows test readings for the circuit with the trouble ticket, charted against normal limits and earlier tests, so no printouts are compared by hand. Earlier trouble reports for the same line appear in the same view. Deciding repair needs and methods stays with the technician; the repair plan uses fixed fields on the work order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Printouts, spreadsheets and ticket histories sat in separate places.
tasks.enabler_now: Network management systems chart readings against limits next to ticket history.
tasks.still_hard: Readings within limits can still hide a fault.
tasks.human_edge: Reading a slow drift that no single threshold shows.

reach.learn: Whether linked histories speed up diagnosis.

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy offers work orders that fill themselves in and checklists for technicians.
Network management systems chart test readings against limits and history.

assumptions: Boundary: from the trouble ticket to the repair plan; the repair is outside.
Input contract: tickets from the help desk; readings from the network management system; limits set by the network engineering team; fallback is printouts.

Deciding repairs keeps its full time. s1 keeps 40 for readings not in the system; s2 keeps 60 for reading the reports; s3 keeps 50 for reading the chart and flagged deviations; s5 keeps 85 because the fields set the layout and the technician still writes the plan.
Readings are kept per circuit, not per technician.

incremental.description: Telecom technician reports wrong limits to network engineering.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an older circuit without stored test history, so readings are still collected and compared by hand (14.7); high: circuits monitored with history and limits (31.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The telecom technician keeps troubleshooting, cable judgement and repair decisions; phone queues, paper records and manual look-ups shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technician who spends saved time on recurring faults.

job.title: Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers, Except Line Installers
